findings.title: unsubscribe action crashes when no TopicUser record exists
findings.body: In TopicsController#unsubscribe, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil for any logged-in user who can see the topic but has never had a TopicUser row created for it (e.g. never visited it and never received an email about it, since TopicUser is normally created lazily). The very next line calls `tu.notification_level` with no nil check, which raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil`, producing a 500 error for any such request (e.g. someone directly navigating to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe for a topic they haven't interacted with).

findings.title: Notification-level mutation performed as a side effect of a plain GET request, with no idempotency or CSRF protection
findings.body: The new `unsubscribe` action (routed via GET in config/routes.rb lines 440-441) mutates `TopicUser#notification_level` directly inside a GET request handler, with no confirmation step and no CSRF protection (GET requests are not covered by Rails' CSRF token checks). Because the action is keyed off the logged-in session (current_user) rather than a signed one-time token (unlike the existing key-based `email/unsubscribe/:key` route), any page that causes the user's browser to issue a GET to this URL while they are logged in (e.g. an tag, link prefetching, or an email security scanner following the link) can silently change their notification settings. Additionally, the mutation is not idempotent: every visit to the same URL re-evaluates `tu.notification_level > regular` using the *current* (already mutated) value, so repeated visits (page refresh, back/forward navigation, duplicate email link clicks, or automated re-fetching) progressively downgrade watching/tracking -> regular -> muted, fully muting the topic after just two visits even though the user only intended a single click.

findings.title: Direct TopicUser save bypasses the canonical TopicUser.change path
findings.body: The new action mutates `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly instead of using `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`, which is the method used everywhere else in the codebase (e.g. TopicsController#set_notifications) for this kind of update. This bypasses: setting `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id`, publishing the `/topic/#{topic_id}` MessageBus event (so any other open tab/browser showing the topic will not reflect the new notification state in real time), and the `observe_after_save_callbacks_for` hook (e.g. UserActionObserver). This creates an inconsistent code path for notification-level changes and a real-time UI sync gap.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation now silently requires an unsubscribe_url interpolation value
findings.body: `config/locales/server.en.yml`'s `unsubscribe_link` key now contains `%{unsubscribe_url}`, which `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` (used in both `html_part` at line 67 and `body` at line 90) will try to interpolate. `template_args` only contains `:unsubscribe_url` if the caller of `build_email`/`MessageBuilder.new` passed it in `opts`. Currently only `send_notification_email` in user_notifications.rb supplies it alongside `add_unsubscribe_link: true`, but this is an implicit, unenforced contract: any other current or future caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` at email-build time, breaking that notification email entirely.

findings.title: "stop_notifications" message is inaccurate when the user was watching/tracking the topic
findings.body: The text "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>" is shown unconditionally by the unsubscribe page/controller, but the backend logic in TopicsController#unsubscribe (lines 107-111) only sets notification_level to `muted` when it was already `regular` or below; if the user was `tracking` or `watching`, it is merely downgraded to `regular`, which still generates notifications for mentions/replies. The displayed copy therefore overstates the actual effect for a large class of users (anyone above 'regular'), who will continue to receive some notifications despite being told they will 'stop receiving notifications'.

findings.title: Typo in computed property name 'stopNotificiationsText'
findings.body: The property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (extra 'i', missing proper spelling of 'Notifications') instead of `stopNotificationsText`. It is referenced consistently with the same typo in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs line 3, so it works, but the misspelling makes the code harder to find/search/maintain and looks unprofessional in a user-facing feature.

findings.title: No controller spec coverage for the new unsubscribe action
findings.body: The new TopicsController#unsubscribe action introduces non-trivial logic (slug-mismatch redirect, JSON vs HTML handling, toggling notification_level based on current state, and a dependency on an existing TopicUser row) but no corresponding spec file changes are included in this PR (no updates to spec/controllers/topics_controller_spec.rb). Given the nil-TopicUser crash risk and the notification-level toggling logic described above, this feature ships without any automated regression protection.

findings.title: No assertion that the new unsubscribe_url renders in the email body/html_part
findings.body: The test was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to `Email::MessageBuilder.new`, but none of the existing assertions check that this value actually appears in `message_with_unsubscribe.body` or `html_part` output. The only existing assertion still just checks for `user_preferences_url`. This leaves the new per-topic unsubscribe link functionality (the actual feature of this PR) without direct test coverage, and would not catch the `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` risk described above if `unsubscribe_url` were ever omitted by a caller.

findings.title: No test added for new Topic#unsubscribe_url helper
findings.body: The new `unsubscribe_url` method on Topic (returning `"#{url}/unsubscribe"`) has no accompanying unit test verifying its output format, despite being a new public API used both by the mailer and the controller's redirect logic.
